claims.head: Slavin and Chatfield get the Strome assignment
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ P2 (Slavin and Chatfield) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Capitals’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Slavin and Chatfield out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Capitals’ second line is Leonard, Strome and Kyrou.
claims.nums: At home: 43% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 24% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Capitals’ second line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Carolina home games this season · 3 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Carolina’s P2 (Slavin and Chatfield) at home: 43% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ second lines. Matchups, Carolina home games this season, 3 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face second lines about 24% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: Don’t buy Kochetkov’s slump against the Capitals
claims.body: Kochetkov has been shaky against the Capitals since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Washington: .869 save percentage · .905 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Kochetkov’s record against the Capitals.
claims.call: If Kochetkov starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .905 than to his .869 against the Capitals.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Washington, 2,296 shots against everyone else

chips.tip: Kochetkov: .869 save percentage in 6 starts against Washington since 2023-24.
Kochetkov: .905 save percentage against everyone else since 2023-24, on 2,296 shots.

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: Penalties could cost the Capitals
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ power play creates at least their usual 8.2 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Capitals’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Hurricanes’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Capitals tonight. The Capitals take a lot of penalties and the Hurricanes draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

notes.text: Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 53% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 65 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should be favored
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Capitals’ best way in is getting good looks.

WSH.head: The Capitals are up against it
WSH.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Capitals can start with getting good looks, plus Logan Thompson stealing the show.

story.head: The Hurricanes are on a heater
paras: The Capitals already played in Carolina once this season and left with a 5-2 win. The Hurricanes are on a tear, five straight wins. The Capitals are 3-2-0.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Capitals’ second line. Don’t read much into Kochetkov’s record against the Caps.
